A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEAP research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original MEAP-versus-NTP pre-training and fine-tuning experiments, retrieval and summarization evaluations, masking ablations, and attention analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for additional base models, hallucination judges, and masking strategies.

M1.justification: The proposed random-masking pre-training and duplicated-sequence fine-tuning procedures retain their masking rates and answer-length gate. Masked-answer prediction, emphasized in v2 Section 3, was already specified in v1 Section 4.2. The revised equation does not establish an implemented algorithm change; span masking appears as an ablation alternative.

E1.justification: The same commonsense, needle retrieval, MDQA, M-RS, and summarization tasks remain, alongside SlimPajama context extension and Alpaca fine-tuning. NaturalQuestions-Open is newly identified as the source for existing MDQA coverage. Additional base models and judges change settings rather than datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: NTP remains the baseline in retained comparisons. New Table 15 additionally compares default random masking against 5-Span Mask and 50-Span Mask. The additional base models and hallucination judges are experimental settings and evaluators, respectively, rather than new competing algorithms.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands experimental settings through Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B-0.2, and Qwen2.5-14B fine-tuning comparisons, Qwen-Plus and GPT-4o hallucination judges, and a 0.3B-model/5B-token masking-strategy experiment. Section 4.1.2 also corrects 80B to 60B, matching the unchanged Table 2; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained masking-rate and attention analyses, v2 adds architecture/scale generalizability checks in Tables 6–7, evaluation across additional judges in Table 4, and random-versus-span masking tests in Section 6.1/Table 15. Together these substantially broaden checks on whether benefits depend on the base model, evaluator, or masking pattern.

E5.justification: v1 Table 8 reports descriptive attention changes only; v2 Table 10 adds t-statistics and p-values below 1e-6 for all four comparisons. The stated 500-sequence sample remains unchanged. No increased training-run count, seed reporting, or confidence intervals are established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical evidence in Tables 4, 6, 7, and 15 while retaining matched earlier scores. For example, new Table 7 reports Llama-3.2-3B MDQA averages of 13.05 for NTP and 21.96 for MEAP. Table 15 reports MDQA scores of 0.218 for random masking versus 0.168 and 0.189 for 5- and 50-token spans.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces the fine-tuning likelihood product over all positions with a negative-log objective indexed by Uq union Um and defines copied-token notation. This is a limited formal revision, although the union remains inconsistent with the prose restricting loss to masked answer tokens. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: simple MLM–NTP integration, improved retrieval and long-context reasoning, preserved language-modeling performance, and training efficiency. The headline 11.77-point fine-tuning MDQA improvement is unchanged. New experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: New Section 4.2.2 interprets the additional model results as evidence of effectiveness across architectures and sizes. Section 5 adds a connection between MEAP's attention mechanism and sparse-attention research. Existing mechanism explanations remain, and no substantive new limitations discussion appears.

D1.justification: Section 4.1.3 newly documents MDQA's NaturalQuestions-Open provenance, construction using one answer document plus answer-free distractors, and use of 64K-extended models. The Siflow platform disclosure is removed. The printed repository address in v2 points to the same hyperlink already embedded in v1, so code access is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Nelson et al., Kwiatkowski et al., Hurst et al., and Martins et al., including a brief substantive connection to sparse attention. The broader positioning relative to MLM, NTP, UniLM, and UL2 remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include targeted revisions to the fine-tuning description, an expanded MDQA explanation, new generalizability and masking-strategy subsections, and publication-footer and citation edits. The main section order and most prose remain intact; this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6, 7, and 15, expands Table 4 with judge-specific rows, and restructures the attention-statistics table. Figure 3 receives a corrected caption. Existing figure graphics remain unchanged, while several displays and appendix tables move within the retained layout.

improvement.justification: The additional base-model, judge, and masking-pattern checks reduce dependence on choices insufficiently tested in v1, while attention significance reporting and clearer MDQA construction strengthen the evidence and documentation. These provide a limited net improvement around the retained contribution. Sparse details for the new runs and inconsistent fine-tuning loss notation remain unresolved.
